newsitem.title: GERMANY: Deutsche Bahn 96 group pretax profit rises 25 pct.
newsitem.headline: Deutsche Bahn 96 group pretax profit rises 25 pct.

text.p: German railway Deutsche Bahn AG said on Wednesday that 1996 group pretax profit rose 25 percent to 693 million marks ($414.7 million) on a 1.3 percent rise in group sales to 30.2 billion marks.

The state-owned company said it expected sales to rise in 1997 but profits would remain unchanged because of investments in a telecommunications venture. The sale of a 49.8 percent stake in its DBKom telecoms unit to Mannesmann AG contributed 200 million marks to profits last year. ($ = 1.671 German Marks)
Deutsche Bahn 96 group pretax profit rises 25 pct

Railroad revenue in 1996 rose 1.7 percent to 24.1 billion marks. Local passenger traffic generated revenue of 11 billion marks, up 3.7 percent, while long distance travel contributed 5.4 billion marks, up 3.8 percent.
Freight revenue fell 6.5 percent to 7.1 billion marks.
Railroad pretax profit was more than 300 million marks, up from more than 200 million marks in 1995, Deutsche Bahn said without providing more precise figures.
The number of employees in the group fell to 288,485, down 24,094 from the end of 1995.

Deutsche Bahn was expected later on Wednesday to name Johannes Ludewig, state secretary in the German Economics Ministry, to succeed chief executive Heinz Duerr. Duerr is due to step down in July and become chairman of the railroad's supervisory board.
